subject.title: macOS: Gateway daemon PATH excludes user bin dirs (nix, bun, local, etc.)

question: Should macOS Gateway LaunchAgents keep the canonical minimal PATH, add an explicit operator opt-in for user bin directories, or include user bins by default?
rationale: Current code and tests preserve a hardened LaunchAgent PATH, while the Nix docs and reporter describe a real tool-discovery gap; automation should not choose the command-resolution trust boundary.

options.title: Keep minimal default with opt-in
options.body: Preserve the current safe default and add an explicit, documented service PATH opt-in only after schema, doctor, docs, and security tests are agreed.

options.title: Change macOS default
options.body: Include macOS user-bin directories by default and require fresh-install plus upgrade proof for the broader command-resolution surface.

options.title: Decline service PATH expansion
options.body: Keep daemon PATH policy unchanged and fix the Nix docs or route users to exec PATH controls and stable system install locations.

recommendation.title: Keep minimal default with opt-in
recommendation.body: Preserve the current safe default and add an explicit, documented service PATH opt-in only after schema, doctor, docs, and security tests are agreed.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is the clearest recent owner signal for managed service PATH precedence and package-manager PATH hardening.
